Reason for Admission:
Acute onset right upper quadrant pain.

Medical History:
The patient was diagnosed with primary hypogammaglobulinemia and was receiving monthly intra-venous immunoglobulin (IVIG). She had a surgical history of parathyroidectomy, open cholecystectomy, and a caesarian section.

Hospital Course:
Upon presentation to the emergency room, a computerized tomography (CT) scan revealed a chronic ventral hernia containing fat anterior to the left lobe of the liver. The hernia was successfully reduced through judicious use of analgesia, and two weeks later, the patient underwent a laparoscopic transabdominal pre-peritoneal (TAPP) mesh repair. Viable incarcerated omentum and a falciform ligament hernia extending into the abdominal wall in the epigastrium were discovered during laparoscopic visualization. The hernia neck was closed laparoscopically with an intra-corporeal V-loc™ suture, and the defect was covered with an underlay Ventralite™ mesh secured with Absorbatac™ staples. Her post-operative recovery was uneventful, and she was discharged home the same day.

Follow-Up Instructions:
The patient is advised to follow up with her primary care physician and surgeon to monitor for any complications or signs of recurrence.

Patient: 48 years old female
Admission date: [Date]
Discharge date: [Date]
Diagnosis: Hepatoid adenocarcinoma originated from adrenal gland

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted with the diagnosis of stage 5 hydatic cyst in the liver. The patient underwent an FDG18 Positron Emition Tomography which revealed a 4 x 5 cm mass near the right lobe cyst and it was invaded to diaphragmatic crura. The patient underwent segment 6-7 hepatectomy and diaphragmatic resection. The tumor was composed of medium-sized polygonal cells with granular eosinophilic cytoplasm with no tumor cells in the liver parenchyma close to the tumor. Immunohistochemical stains were performed which suggested a hepatoid adenocarcinoma originated from adrenal gland. The patient was discharged on the fifth day after surgery.

Treatment:
The patient was given adjuvant therapy with 5-flourousil and gemcitabine for 6 months and radiotherapy with the dose of 4500 cGy for 5.

Condition on Discharge:
The patient was discharged in good condition with instructions to continue with the prescribed treatment plan and to follow up with the appropriate healthcare provider.

Patient Name: [Redacted]
Age: 69 years
Gender: Female
Admission Date: [Redacted]
Discharge Date: [Redacted]
Diagnosis: High grade leiomyosarcoma

Hospital Course:
The patient presented with a progressively enlarging mass in her left buttock that was believed to have a smooth muscle origin. A needle biopsy was performed, and the mass was found to be a well-differentiated spindle cell sarcoma with pleomorphic areas. Surgery was scheduled, and a laminectomy was performed to access the posterior vaginal wall tumor. The tumor, including the capsule, was completely resected. The histopathological and immunohistochemical results confirmed that the tumor was a high grade leiomyosarcoma. The patient received adjuvant chemotherapy after surgery and was free of disease at a one-year follow-up.

Summary:
A 69-year-old Chinese woman with a four-month history of a progressively enlarging mass in her left buttock was diagnosed with high grade leiomyosarcoma. A laminectomy was performed to completely resect the tumor, and adjuvant chemotherapy was administered after surgery. The patient was free of disease at a one-year follow-up and her general condition was good.
